inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 10-Q diluted share count (236.6M, down from 244.0M at FY2025 after ~$1.24B of H1-26 repurchases). Held FLAT: SBC (incl. equity-award withholding) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-count. Period-end count is likely slightly lower if the buyback continued after June; not credited.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL FY2025 cash-flow SBC add-back $53M plus $15M FY2025 share repurchases treated as tax withholding on net-share settlement (Xylem's FY2013-FY2025 repurchase line is small and recurring, consistent with withholding; no combined figure published). The H1-2026 $1,243M repurchase is a genuine buyback, not comp.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build: 10y UST ~4.3%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0-1.1 (water-technology industrial, roughly half municipal non-discretionary) -> cost of equity ~9.5%; pre-tax debt ~5% (3.9% after tax) at ~10% of EV -> WACC ~9.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality, M&A integration and data-center risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost sits inside operating expenses, so it is already inside EBITDA (treatment B by construction). total_debt is borrowings only; operating lease liabilities excluded from net debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial NCI; flows treated as attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (operating company, industrial/moderately cyclical) - Xylem is a pumps/treatment/metering manufacturer and services business whose value is its free cash flow; no bank/REIT/LIC/holdco features. No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry, so this is a fresh build. EBITDA BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is pre-SBC and on a CASH-CONVERSION basis, deliberately below the company's adjusted EBITDA margin (FY25 ~22.2%, FY26 guide 23.1-23.5%) and below GAAP EBITDA+SBC (FY25 20.5%). Reason: a GAAP component build of FY2025 gives ~$1.2bn of unlevered FCF against $910M reported; the ~$250M gap is recurring restructuring/special-charge cash, pension and other operating outflows that Xylem incurs every year (FY23-25 each show a $245-268M gap between NI+D&A+SBC and OCF). The year-1 margin of 18.5% is calibrated so FY2026 owner FCF (~$1.03bn, ~11.2% of revenue) sits just above FY2025's $842M owner FCF, consistent with H1-26 FCF +30% YoY. D&A: 6.4% of revenue in FY2025 is inflated by Evoqua acquired-intangible amortization; it glides to ~4.5% as that amortizes off, which raises the cash tax burden over time. WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer, wc_capture negative (growth consumes ~18-20% of incremental revenue). PORTFOLIO MOVES: the pending Cornell/Roper Pump acquisition ($1.46bn, announced 2026-08-11) and WaterFleet (~$200M) are excluded from both the flows and the bridge (assumed bought at roughly NPV-neutral prices); the AURELIUS international-metering sale is reflected only via the FY2026 ~2% reported-growth guide. The Q2-26 debt rise to $2.93bn funded the H1-26 buyback and TriOS, and is in net debt. BUYBACKS: Xylem is now a genuine repurchaser ($1.24bn H1-26); per method they are value-neutral here, and the lower share count is captured in the anchor.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: organic revenue growth (FY2025 +5.5% reported, FY2026 guide ~2% reported / 2-3% organic, Q2-26 orders +42%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (31% 5yr, 49% 3yr) diverges far more than 30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs because the May-2023 Evoqua acquisition was paid in stock (~$7bn of equity issued, shares 180M -> 242M). Every historical CAGR is acquisition-inflated; none is a forward organic rate. Selected 5.0% organic instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not deducted as Xylem is net debt). Owner FCF: FY2020 615, FY2022 351, FY2025 842 (FY2025 owner basis includes $15M equity-award withholding; earlier years SBC only). The 3yr FCF CAGR starts from a depressed FY2022 (supply-chain working-capital build) and overstates trend. SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are close: SBC is small (~0.6-0.8% of revenue) and not outgrowing cash flow.

base.narrative: FY26 at guide (~2% reported, metering divestiture drag); record Q2-26 orders convert into 5-5.5% organic growth FY27-28 on municipal replacement, PFAS treatment and data-center cooling; cash-basis margin climbs 250bp as restructuring cash fades and mix improves, then holds.

bull.narrative: Data-center/semiconductor water becomes a durable second leg and PFAS compliance capex peaks into the early 2030s; organic growth runs 7-8% for three years; portfolio pruning plus Evoqua synergies take the cash-basis margin to ~22.6%.

bear.narrative: Hyperscaler capex pauses and the order surge proves pull-forward; municipal budgets slip; Applied Water follows the industrial cycle down; the Cornell/Roper and WaterFleet integrations absorb the margin program so the cash-basis margin barely moves.

scenario_narratives.base: Xylem delivers its FY2026 guide (~$9.2bn revenue, adj. EBITDA margin 23.1-23.5%) and converts the record Q2-26 backlog (orders +42%) into mid-single-digit organic growth through FY2028, carried by non-discretionary US municipal replacement, PFAS treatment upgrades and data-center cooling/water reuse. The margin program (price, productivity, divesting the dilutive international metering business) lifts cash conversion steadily as restructuring cash fades. Growth decays to GDP-plus by year 10.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data-center, semiconductor and life-sciences water demand becomes a durable second engine rather than a cyclical spike, PFAS deadlines drive a multi-year treatment capex wave, and Xylem's unique pumps-treatment-metering-analytics breadth wins system-level contracts. Organic growth runs 7-8% for three years and portfolio simplification plus software attach (Xylem Vue) push margins ~150bp above base.
scenario_narratives.bear: The order surge is AI-capex pull-forward that fades with a hyperscaler slowdown; FY2026's trimmed revenue guide proves the leading indicator, with gains margin-only. Municipal funding slips, Applied Water tracks a weak industrial cycle, and a dense M&A calendar (TriOS, WaterFleet, Cornell/Roper on top of Evoqua) under a new CFO soaks up management bandwidth and rising leverage, leaving margins flat and growth at 2-3%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): leverage is rising into four overlapping deals under a new CFO and the data-center leg is unproven. Base 50%: guidance credibility is good (EPS guide raised twice) and half the revenue is non-discretionary municipal. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs both a durable data-center vertical and clean integration to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Xylem on owner FCF from a component build calibrated to the cash it actually converts, not to adjusted EBITDA. The company's adjusted figures exclude ~2pp of recurring restructuring and special charges that have been cash every year since the Evoqua deal; capitalizing adjusted EBITDA would overstate the business. Acquisitions are treated as NPV-neutral and excluded from both flows and bridge.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash conversion: if restructuring/special cash charges do not fade, the 250bp margin ramp in base does not happen
Data-center order durability (Q2-26 orders +42% vs revenue +2%)
M&A integration and leverage: Cornell/Roper ($1.46bn) not yet in net debt; if overpaid, value falls by the excess
D&A glide: falling acquired-intangible amortization raises cash tax over the horizon
Terminal value share is high for a 9% WACC / 3% growth build; the 18x cap is close to binding
